metadata.title: Treylon Burks (foot) limited in practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Treylon Burks was limited in practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Burks was limited out of the bye week with a foot injury. He is in line for an expanded role if he is healthy with Terry McLaurin out for the season.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks - Limited by foot injury Wednesday
metadata.description: Burks (foot) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Burks was injured toward the end of Washington's Week 6 loss to the 49ers two Monday nights ago, but he was at least able to get in a limited session coming out of the bye week. With Terry McLaurin (knee) done for the year, Burks is expected to take on a larger role, along with rookie Antonio Williams, behind Stefon Diggs (hand) at wide receiver.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks in Line for Uptick in Playing Time in Washington
metadata.description: Washington Commanders wide receiver Treylon Burks should be in line for an uptick in playing time going forward after Terry McLaurin suffered a season-ending knee injury in the Week 6 loss to the San Francisco 49ers last Monday night. Burks played 55.2% of the offensive snaps against the 49ers and caught four of his six targets for a season-high 66 yards in the 23-17 loss. The 26-year-old's receptions and targets were also season highs in the same game that McLaurin went down with an injury, which is not a coincidence. Veteran Stefon Diggs should operate as quarterback Jayden Daniels' go-to passing-game target, but both Burks and rookie Antonio Williams should have added responsibilities, starting in Week 8 in their Sunday night showdown against the division-rival Philadelphia Eagles. Burks, a former 18th overall pick by the Tennessee Titans in 2022 from Arkansas, has caught only nine of 17 targets this year for 152 yards, but he has found the end zone twice and should be a waiver-wire target in deeper leagues this week. He is currently rostered in just 1% of Yahoo leagues.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks an Interesting Waiver Target After Teammate's Injury
metadata.description: Washington Commanders wide receiver Treylon Burks had his best game of the season in the Monday night loss to the San Francisco 49ers, and it was not a coincidence that it came in the same game in which Terry McLaurin suffered a season-ending knee injury. Burks played 55% of the offensive snaps and caught four of his six targets for 66 yards in the 23-17 loss on the road in the Bay Area. The 26-year-old former 18th overall pick by the Tennessee Titans in 2022 from Arkansas now has nine grabs on the year in five games for 152 yards and two touchdowns, and with McLaurin now out for the rest of the season, he should have a regular role in three-wide sets alongside Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams. Burks ended up being a massive bust for the Titans, but he looked better in his limited time (eight games) with Washington last year and is definitely on pace for a career year in D.C. in 2026 now that McLaurin is done for the season. He is more of a deep-league waiver-wire target and is not currently rostered in any Yahoo leagues. In Burks' first year in the NFL with the Titans, he had 33 catches for 444 yards and one touchdown in 11 games (six starts).

metadata.title: Treylon Burks - Season-best marks in catches, yards Monday
metadata.description: Burks finished with four receptions for 66 yards on six targets in Monday's 23-17 loss to the 49ers.
metadata.analysis: The reception, yardage and target totals were all season-best totals for Burks, whose heightened involvement in the passing game may have been a byproduct of No. 1 wideout Terry McLaurin (knee) exiting the game late in the first quarter. Though Burks didn't see a major spike in playing time compared to prior weeks -- he was on the field for 37 of 67 offensive snaps (55.2 percent) -- he should be able to maintain a regular role in three-receiver sets alongside Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams, with McLaurin expected to miss time and potentially even being sidelined for the rest of the season.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks goes for 66 yards in Week 6
metadata.description: Treylon Burks caught four of his six targets for 66 yards in a 23-17 loss to the 49ers in Week 6.
metadata.analysis: Burks finished second on the Commanders in receiving yards behind only Chig Okonkwo. The veteran receiver saw an expanded role after Terry McLaurin suffered a knee injury in the first half and was carted off the field. Burks will have some flex appeal in Week 8 after his Week 7 bye, assuming McLaurin can't play.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks - Ready for Week 6
metadata.description: Burks (shoulder) doesn't have a designation for Monday's game in San Francisco.
metadata.analysis: Burks practiced in a limited capacity during the entirety of Week 6 prep due to a shoulder issue, but it won't stop him from being available Monday. Fellow WR Stefon Diggs (hamstring) is listed as questionable, and if he's inhibited or sidelined this week, Burks will stand to benefit in the Commanders' passing game. In four contests this season, Burks has notched five catches (on 11 targets) for 86 yards and two touchdowns.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks - Still limited Friday
metadata.description: Burks (shoulder) remained limited in Friday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) upgraded to limited after being DNP on Thursday, and Terry McLaurin got a veteran's rest day after returning from his hamstring injury last Sunday. Burks caught two of five targets for 26 yards in last Sunday's 27-27 tie with the Giants.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks (shoulder) listed as limited Thursday
metadata.description: Treylon Burks (shoulder) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: A shoulder injury left Burks limited at practice on Thursday. It doesn't look like it will leave him sidelined for Week 6, however, and he will again be primed for more work than usual if Stefon Diggs (hamstring) misses another game for Washington.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks - Tending to shoulder issue
metadata.description: Burks was limited at Thursday's practice due to a shoulder injury.
metadata.analysis: After being a healthy scratch in Week 1, Burks has been active and increased his snap share in each of the ensuing four contests, a span in which he combined for a 5-86-2 line on 11 targets. While Burks and No. 1 WR Terry McLaurin (hamstring) both opened Week 6 prep with capped sessions, Stefon Diggs (hamstring) was held out entirely Thursday. If Diggs requires another absence Monday at San Francisco and Burks is active, the latter again should be a regular option for QB Jayden Daniels in the passing game.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks - Season-high five targets in Week 5 tie
metadata.description: Burks caught two passes on five targets for 16 yards during Sunday's 27-27 tie with the Giants.
metadata.analysis: Burks saw a season-high five targets during Sunday's game, which was second-most on the Commanders behind Chig Okonkwo (six). Burks only logged two catches, but his season was a 13-yard pass late in overtime that set the Commanders up well within field-goal range, only for Jayden Daniels to mismanage the clock to end the game on a tie. Burks has a 5-86-2 receiving line on 10 targets over his last three games, though his scoring floor would take a considerable hit if Stefon Diggs (hamstring) is cleared to play in the Commanders' Week 6 road game against the 49ers on Monday.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks quiet in Week 5
metadata.description: Treylon Burks caught two of his five targets for 26 yards in the Commanders' 27-27 tie against the New York Giants in Week 5.
metadata.analysis: Burks remains one of many non-factors in the Washington passing attack to begin the season, finishing with under 50 receiving yards in each of his four contests. The wideout can be left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 6 contest against the San Francisco 49ers.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks (shoulder) logs full practice Thursday
metadata.description: Treylon Burks (shoulder) logged a full practice session on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: As expected, Burks was able to log another full practice session on Thursday. His shoulder injury isn't serious and he is expected to play through it this week, and he may see more work than usual against the Giants with Terry McLaurin (hamstring) and Stefon Diggs (hamstring) both at risk of being sidelined for that matchup.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks (shoulder) fully practices Wednesday
metadata.description: Treylon Burks (shoulder) fully practiced for the Commanders on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Burks was dealing with some kind of a shoulder injury following Week 4, but it's not a serious issue and didn't prevent him from logging a full practice this week. Look for him to continue to contribute on this offense moving forward, though he won't have much fantasy value for the foreseeable future.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks' Big-Play Upside Worth a Waiver Claim?
metadata.description: Washington Commanders wide receiver Treylon Burks has scored a touchdown in back-to-back games, putting him on the fantasy radar in leagues with 12+ teams. Burks saw a season-high 59% snap share in Week 4, and his bigger role was a direct result of Terry McLaurin (hamstring) being inactive. The 26-year-old was targeted three times, and although he only caught one pass, it went for a 47-yard touchdown reception. He has now scored a touchdown in back-to-back games, totaling 21.0 fantasy points in PPR leagues during that two-week span. The reception volume has been quite low, but we like his chances of having more catchable balls thrown his way with Jayden Daniels (elbow) trending toward playing in Week 5 against the New York Giants. The biggest factor for Burks' outlook is the status of McLaurin, who remains up in the air for this week. It'll be a little while before we get more clarity on McLaurin's status. In the meantime, managers in 12+ team leagues should consider adding Burks as a high-ceiling fantasy receiver.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks - Produces long TD in London loss
metadata.description: Burks caught one of three targets for a 47-yard touchdown in Sunday's 30-13 loss to the Colts.
metadata.analysis: With Terry McLaurin (hamstring) inactive, Burks saw increased snaps in the Commanders' wideout rotation that also involved Stefon Diggs, Dyami Brown and rookie Antonio Williams. Burks saw the fewest targets of the four and made the most of his one grab, breaking off a 47-yard score in the third quarter. If McLaurin continues to miss time, Burks should see rotational playing time at wideout, but he's not currently a playable fantasy option.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks finds the end zone in Week 4
metadata.description: Treylon Burks caught 1-of-3 targets for 47 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders loss to the Colts.
metadata.analysis: Burks caught the first touchdown of rookie QB Athan Kaliakmanis' career, the lone touchdown for the Commanders' offense Sunday. Fantasy managers should still view Burks as an option only in deeper leagues.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks a Deep League Flier in Week 4
metadata.description: Washington Commanders wide receiver Treylon Burks is expected to see more snaps in Week 4 against the Indianapolis Colts, with Terry McLaurin (hamstring) not expected to play. Burks ran the third most routes behind McLaurin and Stefon Diggs in Week 3 against Seattle and hauled in both of his targets last week for 13 yards and a touchdown. The 26-year-old is likely to share some routes with Dyami Brown and others as Washington rotates their wide receivers a bit. Despite a likely increased role, Burks doesn't project as a fantasy option for Week 4 except for deeper leagues. He is worth considering as a high-risk, high-upside option in DFS competitions given the increase in snaps.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks catches touchdown in Week 3 win
metadata.description: Treylon Burks caught both of his targets for 13 yards and one touchdown in the Commanders' 33-31 win over the Seattle Seahawks in Week 3.
metadata.analysis: Burks has made minimal impact in the Washington passing attack early on, finishing with less than 15 receiving yards in each of his two games. The wideout remains difficult to trust in all formats ahead of a Week 4 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks - Held without catch in Week 2
metadata.description: Burks failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 37-20 loss to the Cowboys.
metadata.analysis: After being inactive in the season opener against the Eagles, Burks played 21 offensive snaps against Dallas as the fifth receiver behind Terry McLaurin, Stefon Diggs, Dyami Brown and rookie Antonio Williams. Burks doesn't have any fantasy value in redraft formats at the moment.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks - Won't play against Philadelphia
metadata.description: Burks (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Eagles.
metadata.analysis: Burks appeared in eight of the Commanders' final nine games of the 2025 regular season after being released by the Titans in October. However, the 2022 first-rounder will join Luke McCaffrey (coach's decision) in street clothes Sunday, with the Commanders opting for five active wide receivers for game day. Burks' next chance to play is Week 2 against the Cowboys on Sunday, Sept. 20.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks Inactive Ahead of Week 1 Battle vs. Eagles
metadata.description: Washington Commanders wide receiver Treylon Burks was listed as inactive shortly before his team's Week 1 tilt against the host Philadelphia Eagles, the team reported via the X platform. The 26-year-old dealt with foot soreness during training camp, but it hasn't yet been confirmed if that is the reason he isn't playing in Sunday's game. The former first-round pick played just eight games in 2025 after fracturing his collarbone in the offseason, and finished the campaign with 10 receptions for 130 yards and one touchdown. The Commanders' receiving room has gotten crowded thanks to the addition of Stefon Diggs, who is expected to get plenty of playing time opposite Terry McLaurin this year. Burks' absence from Sunday's game in Philadelphia further reinforces that he doesn't produce enough weekly fantasy volume to be a reliable asset in redraft leagues.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks Faces a Tougher Road to Consistent Targets
metadata.description: Washington Commanders wide receiver Treylon Burks had a good enough summer to put himself back on the fantasy radar, but the receiver room changed around him. Burks was getting legitimate first-team work early in camp after catching only 10 passes for 130 yards and one touchdown in eight games last season. Washington then added Stefon Diggs, who is expected to handle the No. 2 role opposite Terry McLaurin. Burks now sits behind Diggs on the current depth chart, and the Commanders have talked about using him more as a specialized deep threat. That's a much different fantasy outlook than the possible starting job he was chasing earlier in the summer. Luke McCaffrey, Jaylin Lane, Dyami Brown and rookie Antonio Williams only add more competition for whatever targets are left. None of this is really about Burks playing poorly. Dan Quinn praised his speed and work throughout camp, and he clearly earned a spot in the rotation. There just isn't an obvious path to enough weekly volume for Burks to matter outside of deeper leagues.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks Working His Way Back into the Fantasy Conversation
metadata.description: Commanders wide receiver Treylon Burks has had a career defined by injuries and disappointment, but a unique skill set and a solid first training camp in Washington have him well-positioned to earn a role in 2026. The arrival of four-time Pro Bowler Stefon Diggs in early August changed the landscape of the Commanders' receiver room, but Burks' blend of size and speed should allow him to earn a complementary role behind Diggs and top option Terry McLaurin. Still projected as part of a potential rotation with Luke McCaffrey, Jaylin Lane, and 2026 third-round pick Antonio Williams, he is unlikely to suddenly reemerge as a coveted fantasy asset, but in an offense expected to gel with better overall health in its first year under new offensive coordinator David Blough, Burks has the opportunity to work his way into the flex conversation in deeper leagues. A former first-round pick of the Tennessee Titans, Burks has yet to top the 444 receiving yards of his rookie season, but he is at least back on the edge of fantasy radars as RotoBaller's WR109.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks Keeping Himself on the Redraft Radar
metadata.description: Washington Commanders wide receiver Treylon Burks is making a better case for himself than he was a few weeks ago, even if the fantasy ceiling is still pretty low. Burks caught just 10 passes for 130 yards and one touchdown in eight games last season, but he has been one of Washington's more noticeable receivers throughout camp. Dan Quinn said Burks came in leaner and has routinely been one of the team's fastest players in practice, especially on deep and in-breaking routes. He backed that up again during Wednesday's joint practice with Miami, making a tough over-the-shoulder catch from Jayden Daniels with tight coverage. The problem is that Washington added Stefon Diggs on Aug. 7, and the first unofficial depth chart now has Burks behind him. Terry McLaurin and Luke McCaffrey are also listed as starters, with several other receivers still fighting for work. RotoBaller has Burks at WR108, which feels right for now. His camp has helped his chances of sticking in the rotation, but he is still more of a deep-league flier than someone to chase in standard redraft leagues.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks - Back at practice
metadata.description: Burks (foot) returned to Commanders practice Saturday, Zach Selby of the Commanders' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Burks missed Thursday's practice due to a sore foot, but he wasn't held out of action long. That's good news for the 2022 first-round draft pick, as he has an opportunity during training camp to compete for a major role in the offense. Antonio Williams and Luke McCaffrey are among the other players jostling for the No. 2 WR role behind Terry McLaurin in an unsettled Washington receiver corps.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks Misses Practice With Foot Soreness
metadata.description: Washington Commanders wide receiver Treylon Burks (foot) did not practice Thursday because of foot soreness, according to Ben Standig. There was no further update on the severity of the issue. Burks is trying to build on a productive offseason while competing for work behind Terry McLaurin in a receiver room without a settled No. 2. Washington re-signed the former first-round pick in March after he caught 10 passes for 130 yards and one touchdown in eight games last season. Health remains central to his case. Burks has played 35 games through four NFL seasons, with 11 being his career high in any one year. The missed practice is worth tracking, but there is not enough information yet to suggest a longer absence. For now, fantasy managers only need to monitor how quickly he returns and whether he can regain the momentum he built during offseason work.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks - Misses practice with sore foot
metadata.description: Burks missed Thursday's practice with foot soreness, Ben Standig of Big 100 Washington D.C. reports.
metadata.analysis: The 2022 first-round pick is part of what seems to be an open competition for WR roles behind locked-in No. 1 Terry McLaurin. Rumors connect Washington with multiple veteran wideouts, but the current depth chart gives Burks a real shot at a top-three role, competing against the likes of Antonio Williams, Luke McCaffrey, Dyami Brown, Jaylin Lane and Van Jefferson.

metadata.title: Treylon Burks an Intriguing Dynasty Buy-Low Candidate Ahead of 2026
metadata.description: A first-round pick of the Tennessee Titans in 2022, current Washington Commanders wide receiver Treylon Burks was never able to live up to his draft-day pedigree in Tennessee. However, the 26-year-old could have a second chance to establish an NFL career in Washington. After latching on with the Commanders midway through the 2025 season, Burks recorded 10 catches for 130 yards and a touchdown on 22 targets across eight games (three starts). While Burks' numbers do not leap off the page, Washington does not currently have an obvious WR2 behind star wideout Terry McLaurin. Health has been one of the main reasons why Burks has struggled as a pro, as he's missed 33 games across four seasons due to toe, knee, concussion, and collarbone issues. If he can stay on the field in 2026, Burks could establish a role in Washington going forward. Dynasty managers in deeper league formats may be wise to take a low-cost flyer on Burks.
